content.comment_body: I have a battery-powered sensor sending results via WiFi to a [product_name] controller. If the sensor's software loop is set to 500 ms, the results are received correctly by the controller. However, increasing the loop time to 1 second for battery savings causes noticeable delays before the controller registers the data. Is there a way to extend a timeout on the controller to tolerate slower Modbus responses? On my PC Modbus test software, I can set timeouts up to 30 seconds; I would like to achieve similar functionality with the controller.
No, this option is not available.

Hello, it depends on your Modbus setup. If the [product_name] controller acts as the Modbus client, you can configure how frequently it synchronizes with the Modbus server. This information may assist you further.

analysis.insight_summary: The issue involves a sensor sending data at longer intervals to conserve battery, which causes delays in data reception on the [product_name] controller using Modbus. Unlike PC-based Modbus tools with configurable response timeouts, the controller lacks such flexibility, limiting its use in low-power or infrequent sensor scenarios.
analysis.user_expectations: User seeks the ability to adjust Modbus response timeouts on the [product_name] controller to support slower sensor updates, similar to the options available in PC-based utilities.
